title: Not an Infrastructure Guy
style: Indie folk singer-songwriter, sparse acoustic guitar with gently picked strings and open pauses, unhurried sway, slightly raspy male baritone in a mellow close delivery, stacked roomy unprocessed harmonies on the hooks, soft waves beneath the vocal, natural intimate production with space for silence.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Sand still hot beneath our feet
You took your sandals off, I followed
Waves keep washing the words away
Before I can decide to own them

I don’t feel down, just a little tired
Not burned out, not broken
Just standing in the middle of the thing
I used to love building

[Chorus]
I’m not an infrastructure guy
That’s what I ended up doing
Not what I am
Dreamer with an engineer’s name
Watching the tracks I laid
Get shaken and put back again

[Verse 2]
Railways, cities, lines on the map
The thrill was in the drawing
Then the ground moved and everything changed
Now it’s duty and maintenance

Willingness is still there
But the spark has gone quiet
Every day is just another list
Of what has to be fixed

[Chorus]
I’m not an infrastructure guy
That’s what I ended up doing
Not what I am
Dreamer with an engineer’s name
Watching the tracks I laid
Get shaken and put back again

[Bridge]
You said it before I could
“Infrastructure is what you ended up doing…”
And something in me loosened
Like the wind undoing your hairI’ve been writing a novel
That’s the new hyperfocus
They didn’t call you because I was lost
They called you because they know

[Final Chorus (quieter, almost spoken at first)]
I’m not an infrastructure guy
That’s what I ended up doing
Not what I am
Dreamer with an engineer’s name
And right now the only thing
I want to build
Is a story

[Outro]
Waves keep coming
You don’t push
Just walk beside me
Until the light goes
